reasoning: No stats yet, so I'm exploring a category not covered so far: food. Botanical 'not what you think' facts are verifiable, easy to grasp, and surprising enough that people tag friends. I chose a carousel with cards because list-style trivia gets saved and shared. Palette 1 hasn't been used yet, so this tests it. The caption ends with a 'which one surprised you' question to measure comments.
topic: Botanical food surprises: berries, nuts, legal fruits
hook: Foods that are secretly not what you think

slides.title: Bananas are berries
slides.body: Botanically, a berry grows from one flower with one ovary and keeps its seeds inside. Bananas fit. So do grapes and kiwis.
slides.image_prompt: A bunch of ripe yellow bananas beside grapes and a sliced kiwi on a wooden table, soft natural light

slides.title: Strawberries aren't berries
slides.body: The red flesh is swollen flower tissue. Each 'seed' on the outside is really a tiny fruit with its own seed inside.
slides.image_prompt: Extreme macro of a red strawberry surface showing tiny yellow seeds, glossy texture, dark background

slides.title: Peanuts aren't nuts
slides.body: They're legumes, like peas and beans. After flowering, the stalk bends into the soil and the pods grow underground.
slides.image_prompt: Freshly pulled peanut plant with pods hanging from its roots, soil crumbs, green leaves, farm field background

slides.title: Almonds are seeds
slides.body: An almond is the seed of a drupe, the same fruit type as peaches and cherries. Its close relatives are plums and apricots.
slides.image_prompt: Green fuzzy almond fruits on a branch, one split open revealing the almond shell inside, sunny orchard

slides.title: A pineapple is many fruits
slides.body: Each one forms from 100 to 200 flowers that fuse together. Every bumpy 'eye' on the skin was once a separate flower.
slides.image_prompt: Young pineapple on its plant with small purple flowers emerging from its bumpy skin, tropical field

slides.title: Cashews hang off an apple
slides.body: The nut grows below a fleshy 'cashew apple'. Its shell holds an oil that irritates skin, so cashews are never sold in the shell.
slides.image_prompt: Red and yellow cashew apples hanging on a tree, each with a curved grey nut attached at the bottom

slides.title: Rhubarb became a fruit
slides.body: Botanically it's a vegetable stalk. But in 1947 a US customs court ruled it a fruit, because that's how people cook it.
slides.image_prompt: Bundle of bright red rhubarb stalks next to a rhubarb pie on a rustic kitchen table

slides.title: Tomatoes: legally veggies
slides.body: Botanically a fruit, but in 1893 the US Supreme Court ruled tomatoes vegetables for import taxes in Nix v. Hedden.
slides.image_prompt: Ripe red tomatoes on the vine beside an old wooden gavel on a table, warm vintage light

cta: Follow so you never miss the next one
caption:
Your fruit bowl is lying to you. A banana is a true berry, a strawberry isn't, and every bump on a pineapple was once its own flower.

Some foods even got their label from judges instead of botanists. In 1893 the US Supreme Court decided the tomato was a vegetable.

Which one surprised you the most?
